configuration: Five-day, one-thread, binary64 Mozambique regional routing run with analytic daily runoff, a tidal boundary, floodplain and bifurcation flow, and uniform 1.5 m levees at fraction 0.4 of each active floodplain profile.
observable: Final-cell river outflow, flood depth, flood storage, protected-side levee storage, and protected-side levee depth
runtime_note: under 300 s; SAB_DAYS shortens or extends the routed window
default_vs_upstream: shortened official t01 levee configuration on the official Mozambique regional map, with generated inputs
variant: The analytic runoff rate is advanced by two binary32 ulps, from 0.0125 to 0.01250000186264515 m/day; this is the smallest input perturbation preserved by the forcing format and probes numerical-noise sensitivity without changing the physical regime.
altbuild: none: the container carries one supported gfortran build configuration, so no independent compiler or floating-point-mode floor is available

comparison.rule: For every listed physical field at every structured-grid cell, require |candidate - reference| <= 1e-3 + 1e-3 * |reference|; grid-cell position is physical, while run metadata, build timings, and storage layout are excluded.

evidence.floor_how: No altbuild is declared; numerical sensitivity is measured by nominal versus the two-ulp forcing variant on Colima arm64 and corroborated by the native TACC x86_64 run.

warrant: The human-approved 1e-3 absolute plus 1e-3 relative bound allows a 0.1% implementation-scale difference in the local-inertial and levee-stage arithmetic while rejecting a wrong levee threshold, omitted protected storage, or materially altered floodplain flux. On Colima arm64, the two-binary32-ulp runoff perturbation used at most 0.0263 of this bound, leaving about 38-fold headroom; the same maximum 32 m3 storage spread appeared in the native TACC x86_64 calibration. The five-day window keeps growth local while including daily runoff and 10-minute tidal updates.
